claims.text: Reducing laser power and scan speed constitutes a low-energy-density LPBF regime for AlCrFeNiSi powder.
The proposed low-energy-density LPBF regime can mitigate residual thermal stresses in miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed regime can improve the mechanical properties of miniature AlCrFeNiSi components relative to conventional high-thermal-load LPBF.
The applicable processing window is limited to components with dimensions below 10 mm.
The proposed regime is applicable under room-temperature build conditions in an inert argon atmosphere.
Reduced LPBF energy input produces lower thermal gradients during layer deposition.
Reduced thermal gradients limit the generation and accumulation of residual stress.
Reduced thermal gradients promote a finer microstructure.
Reduced thermal gradients promote a more homogeneous microstructure.
Lower energy input decreases peak temperatures during LPBF.
Lower energy input reduces rapid-solidification defects.
Lower energy input reduces microstructural inhomogeneity.
Low-energy-density LPBF components will have statistically lower residual stresses than components made under conventional high-thermal-load LPBF conditions.
Low-energy-density LPBF components will have improved tensile properties relative to conventional high-thermal-load LPBF components.
Low-energy-density LPBF components will have improved fatigue properties relative to conventional high-thermal-load LPBF components.
Conventional high-energy LPBF parameters generate high thermal loads and steep cooling rates.
The outcomes may differ for geometries larger than 10 mm or for additive-manufacturing methods other than LPBF.

contradictions.description: The intervention treats simultaneous reductions in laser power and scan speed as a reduction in energy density, while the mechanism assumes lower total energy input. Reduced scan speed alone increases energy delivered per unit scan length, so the claimed lower-energy regime is not established without quantified power, speed, hatch spacing, and layer thickness.
